title: Sold Out in 25 Minutes, a National Museum Turned Pink — BLACKPINK's 'Deadline' Is Rewriting K-pop History
excerpt: BLACKPINK returns after 3 years and 5 months with mini-album Deadline. Pre-orders sold out in 25 minutes, the National Museum of Korea is turning pink — here is everything behind the most talked-about comeback of 2026.
author: MEARROW Editorial Desk
content:
On January 14, YG Entertainment opened pre-orders for BLACKPINK's mini-album *Deadline*. Every version — BLACK Ver., GRAY Ver., MOOD LIGHT Ver. — **sold out within 25 minutes**. Fans had been waiting.

But that was just the beginning. With the official release date of February 27 approaching, BLACKPINK has done something unprecedented in K-pop history: **they've turned South Korea's National Museum of Korea entirely pink.** It marks the first time a government-operated national museum has officially partnered with a K-pop group.

3 years and 5 months of silence. All four members released solo albums on different Western labels. "BLACKPINK is over" became a common refrain. Yet right now, the numbers tell a completely different story.

## 3 Years and 5 Months — Until Deadline

BLACKPINK's last group album was *Born Pink*, released in September 2022. What happened in between reveals just how significant this comeback truly is.

In December 2023, all four members renewed their contracts with YG Entertainment — **for group activities only**. Solo work would be handled by separate Western labels: Jennie with Columbia Records, Lisa with RCA Records, Rose with Atlantic Records, and Jisoo with Warner Records. This "distributed contract" structure was virtually unheard of in K-pop.

Then came the solo rush starting late 2024. Rose's *Rosie* saw her collaboration "APT." with Bruno Mars break into the UK Top 10 — a first for a female K-pop soloist. Lisa's *Alter Ego* debuted at No. 7 on the Billboard 200. Jennie's *Ruby* launched a solo tour, and Jisoo's *Amortage* moved over 200,000 copies in two days. All four proved their individual power, then reunited.

On May 26, 2025, the group comeback was officially confirmed. In July, pre-release single "JUMP" debuted at **No. 1 on both the Billboard Global 200 and Global Excl. U.S. charts simultaneously** — the first song to achieve this in 2025. This also made BLACKPINK the **woman-fronted act with the most No. 1s** on the Global Excl. U.S. chart in its five-year history, surpassing Ariana Grande and Taylor Swift.

## Mini-Album 'Deadline' — The Strategy Behind 5 Tracks

*Deadline* drops on February 27 at 2:00 PM KST. The tracklist:

| # | Track | Notes |
|:-:|-------|-------|
| 1 | JUMP | Pre-release (July 11, 2025) |
| 2 | **GO** | **Title track** (MV same day) |
| 3 | Me and my | - |
| 4 | Champion | - |
| 5 | Fxxxboy | - |

The five-track format drew backlash: "We waited 3.5 years for five songs?" Add leaked tracklists, Bebe Rexha collaboration rumors, and accusations of a "lazy rollout," and the fandom split hard.

A significant behind-the-scenes shift: BLACKPINK switched U.S. distribution from Interscope Records (their partner since 2018) to **The Orchard**. This signals a strategic move toward greater revenue control and distribution autonomy for YG and the group.

## The National Museum Collaboration — Truly Unprecedented

The most jaw-dropping element of this comeback is the **official partnership with the National Museum of Korea**, with Spotify as an official partner. The activation runs from February 27 through March 8, 2026.

Here's what's happening:

**The museum exterior turns pink.** Every day from 4:00 PM to 10:00 PM, the National Museum of Korea's facade and outdoor plaza will be illuminated in BLACKPINK's signature pink lighting. A national museum changing its lighting for a pop group has never happened before.

**A listening zone timed to the album release.** At exactly 2:00 PM on February 27 — the moment the album drops — visitors can hear the full album simultaneously in a dedicated listening space inside the museum.

**Audio guides recorded by the members themselves.** BLACKPINK members narrate guides for 8 key artifacts from the museum's collection. Jisoo and Jennie recorded in Korean, Rose in English, and Lisa will release a Thai-language version in March.

This partnership goes beyond marketing. With BLACKPINK's estimated 100 million global fans, it's a form of **cultural diplomacy** — using K-pop's reach to make Korean history and heritage accessible worldwide. Whether the museum or YG initiated the collaboration hasn't been disclosed, but either way, it's a powerful symbol of how far K-pop's institutional standing has come.

## The Numbers Don't Lie — YG Stock, Tour Revenue, Charts

BLACKPINK's return sent YG Entertainment's stock into overdrive.

| Metric | Figure |
|--------|--------|
| YG stock growth (2025) | **+95.9%** (3rd among global music stocks) |
| Kiwoom Securities target price | **105,000 KRW** |
| Deadline World Tour projected revenue | **~600B KRW (~$440M)** |
| Goyang Stadium (2 shows) gross | **$9.62M** (highest-ever for Asian artist in Korea) |
| Toronto Rogers Stadium (2 shows) | **105,151+ tickets sold** |

YG's stock surged 95.9% in 2025, ranking **third globally** among music stocks — behind only NetEase Cloud Music (+117.1%) and Tencent Music (+100.5%). Kiwoom Securities cited BLACKPINK and BTS's 2026 comebacks as primary growth drivers, raising their target to 105,000 KRW.

However, analysts flag a **revenue concentration risk**. YG's record Q3 2025 profits were driven almost entirely by BLACKPINK. In response, YG launched a 2026 global audition to diversify its artist pipeline.

## Disbandment Rumors, Teaser Backlash — The Fandom Divided

Behind the dazzling numbers, cracks in the fandom are visible.

**Disbandment speculation.** At the Deadline World Tour finale in Hong Kong's Kai Tak Stadium on January 26, all four members were visibly tearful. Rose gave an emotional speech. Social media exploded with "Are they disbanding?" speculation, fueled by reports that YG group contracts expire in 2026. Rose had stated in a November 2024 New York Times interview that "disbanding was never an option," but the anxiety lingered.

**Five-song frustration.** "Five tracks after 3.5 years — is that even trying?" This complaint echoed across both Korean communities and global fandoms. A pre-release tracklist leak made things worse.

**Teaser criticism.** Korean netizens called the Deadline teasers "boring" and "repetitive." Concept photos were dismissed as lacking impact for such a major comeback.

Yet the market doesn't care about fan discourse. 25-minute sellout. Simultaneous Billboard No. 1. A tour projected at $440 million. No matter how divided the fandom gets, the commercial response is overwhelming.

## MEARROW's Perspective on BLACKPINK's Deadline

This comeback represents more than an album release — it showcases a **new business model for the K-pop industry**.

First, the "distributed contract" structure has proven viable. Four members succeeding independently on different Western labels, then reuniting for group synergy — this challenges K-pop's traditional exclusive contract model at its core. Other groups will likely follow this blueprint.

Second, the National Museum partnership signals that **K-pop is being recognized as cultural infrastructure**. It's no longer confined to the "idol music" category. When a national institution extends the invitation, it speaks to a fundamental shift in the industry's standing.

Third, YG's revenue concentration problem is an industry-wide lesson. Over-reliance on a single act is always a risk. For aspiring trainees, though, this structural vulnerability is precisely where opportunity exists — agencies need to diversify, and that means new artists get their chance.

## Looking Ahead

February 27 is seven days away. The album title *Deadline* couldn't be more fitting. The answer to the 3.5-year hiatus, the disbandment rumors, the solo-versus-group debate — everything converges on that date.

When the National Museum of Korea turns pink, BLACKPINK won't just be making a comeback. They'll be **opening the next chapter of K-pop itself**. Whether the album that sold out in 25 minutes can dominate the charts too — 2:00 PM KST on February 27 will tell us everything.
